summary: Implemented packet ws08-s8-imports-core-local-ocr (WS08-S8, DEC-37). New app/ocr.py: local Tesseract (eng+nor) and poppler OCR for scanned PDFs, one job at a time (2 s wait for the slot), an 18 s whole-request deadline, 10 s per binary call, and a page cap from CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_MAX_PAGES (a strict whole number 1 to 50, otherwise 15). It writes one INFO line with page counts and elapsed ms, and nothing from the document or the binaries goes into a log line or an exception. app/chat_extract.py: only in the empty-text branch, and only for a .pdf when CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_ENABLED is exactly 'true'. It returns the OCR text, appends a truncation marker when pages were cut, keeps the 60,000-character check, and sets data.ocr=True. With the switch off the response is unchanged. Dockerfile: one runtime-stage apt line for tesseract-ocr, tesseract-ocr-eng, tesseract-ocr-nor and poppler-utils. docker-compose.yml: two imports-api env lines, CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_ENABLED defaulting to false and CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_MAX_PAGES defaulting to 15. New tests/test_chat_extract_ocr.py covers cases a to j from the brief, plus four extra cases: a busy slot, a missing binary, OCR text that reads as blank, and a non-PDF never reaching OCR. Line endings are kept: ocr.py and the test file are CRLF, chat_extract.py and Dockerfile stay CRLF, and the compose file stays LF. The git footprint is exactly these five files. Two notes.
